tools.name: get_latest_fundamentals
tools.description: The most recent reported value of each metric for one ticker, each with its period (fy, fp), period end, filing date and form. Use it for a company's current figures, or with as_of for what had been filed by a given day. search_companies maps a company name to its ticker. Inputs: ticker (e.g. AAPL, 2330.TW, 005930.KS, 0403091220.BE, 775670417.FR, CC21860.NZC, and 10238429.EE, 5560356163.SE, 47239255.SK, 40003032949.LV where get_coverage lists them, and 96002925948.AU for Australia's tax figures); metric (comma-separated; a name we do not hold is listed in metrics_not_found); as_of (only filings dated on or before that day); compact (true leaves out market_notes and schema). Without a licence key, a company outside the full-history sample answers from its most recent reported fiscal year only (history_depth says so) and as_of is not available. Each metric is its own latest value, so two metrics can come from different periods; a quarterly fp is ONE quarter's figure, not a year; check `stale` (true: the company has filed since without this metric, so the figure is not current). Figures are as filed, each keyed to its filing date (`filed`) as its market records it (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). .TW quarterly values are already SINGLE-QUARTER amounts, so differencing adjacent quarters gives wrong figures. For a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR quarter containing the period end, not the company's fiscal quarter. Each reply's `market_notes` and `schema` state the per-market caveats (solo or group accounts, lawful gaps, charities, flags in `form`). Detailed line items follow local accounting rules and keep the filed sign (capex is negative in Taiwan and Japan); get_data_dictionary defines them per market. The source licences require each reply's `attribution` and `licence` notices to accompany the figures.

metric.description: Comma-separated metrics, e.g. revenue,net_income. Omit for all.

as_of.description: Filing-date cut-off, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2022-01-01). Defaults to today.

compact.description: true leaves out the long per-market notes (market_notes, schema) to save tokens; default false

tools.name: get_fundamentals_history
tools.description: The stored figures for one ticker, one row per metric and period, each with its period (fy, fp), period end, filing date and form. Use it for trends and for what was on file at a past date. Inputs: ticker, metric (comma-separated), from (earliest period end), as_of (only filings dated on or before that day), max_rows (1-250, default 250), compact (true leaves out market_notes and schema). Without a licence key, a company outside the full-history sample answers with its most recent reported fiscal year only: full_history false and history_depth say so, and older filings exist. Long histories are capped at max_rows, keeping the most recent rows of EVERY metric (per_metric says how many of each); metric and from select older rows. Figures are as filed, each keyed to its filing date (`filed`) as its market records it (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). .TW quarterly values are already SINGLE-QUARTER amounts, so differencing adjacent quarters gives wrong figures. For a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR quarter containing the period end, not the company's fiscal quarter. Each reply's `market_notes` and `schema` state the per-market caveats (solo or group accounts, lawful gaps, charities, flags in `form`). Detailed line items follow local accounting rules and keep the filed sign (capex is negative in Taiwan and Japan); get_data_dictionary defines them per market. The source licences require each reply's `attribution` and `licence` notices to accompany the figures.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Look up the ticker for a company name or partial symbol — 'Apple', 'TSMC', '2330', 'samsung', 'LVMH'. Returns up to 8 matches, each with its ticker, name and market; a local subsidiary or a namesake in another country can share a name, and the market tells them apart. market (US, JP, TW, KR, FR, BE, DK, EE, SE, SK, LV, AU, NZC) limits the search to one market. Results with market NZC are New Zealand registered charities, not companies.

tools.description: Markets covered, company counts, history depth per market, the companies that answer with full history without a licence key (full_history_sample), the metric vocabulary, the source attributions that must travel with the data, and the licence the data is supplied under (for a time-limited key, its terms and end date). compact (true) leaves out the per-market notes and accounting descriptions.

tools.name: get_data_dictionary
tools.description: The data dictionary of the detailed line items: for every metric, its definition, which filed line each market reads it from (or why a market has none), and the measured share of that market's company-periods that carry it; the figures we calculate from them, with their formulas; and the rules that apply to all of them (dating, signs, annual-only cash-flow lines, small employers). Use it before comparing a line item across markets, or to learn what a line-item code means. It also defines company.industry and company.status (the register's industry code and legal status, with source and dates), per market. Codes: trade_receivables, trade_and_other_receivables, inventories, trade_payables, trade_and_other_payables, ppe, noncurrent_assets, current_assets, current_liabilities, retained_earnings, depreciation_amortization, interest_expense, cash_flow_operating, capex, minority_interest, temporary_equity, land_and_buildings, land, buildings, pension_provisions, cost_of_materials, purchases_of_goods, purchases_of_materials, wages_and_salaries, operating_taxes, income_tax; calculated: free_cash_flow, working_capital, current_ratio, ebitda.

annotations.title: What each detailed line item means, per market

tools.name: get_company_status
tools.description: The register's legal status of one company: value (active, no_end_recorded, in_restructuring, dissolution_recorded, in_liquidation, bankrupt, dissolved, deregistered), the register's own code and label, since (the date the source gives for it taking effect; null where it gives none), as_of (the date the source stated it) and availability (available, none_stated, not_collected, unavailable, not_in_warehouse). Status is collected for some register markets only (get_data_dictionary's company_attributes lists them); the others answer not_collected. no_end_recorded means the register records no end and no open proceeding; it is not a statement that the company is active. Inputs: ticker; as_of (the status on that day by the source's own dates; needs a licence key).

tools.name: compare_companies
tools.description: The latest filed value of one to 5 metrics for up to 10 companies, side by side, each value with its period (fy, fp, end), filing date, basis (consolidated, solo or reported), unit and source register. Values are as filed, in each company's own currency and unit, never converted; compare fy, fp, end and basis before reading two values together. Inputs: tickers (list), metric (comma-separated, e.g. revenue,net_income), as_of (only filings dated on or before that day; needs a licence key), compact (true leaves out market_notes). Each company counts as one call against the rate limit and, for a key with a company limit, as one company read. Figures are as filed, each keyed to its filing date (`filed`) as its market records it (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). .TW quarterly values are already SINGLE-QUARTER amounts, so differencing adjacent quarters gives wrong figures. For a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR quarter containing the period end, not the company's fiscal quarter. Each reply's `market_notes` and `schema` state the per-market caveats (solo or group accounts, lawful gaps, charities, flags in `form`). Detailed line items follow local accounting rules and keep the filed sign (capex is negative in Taiwan and Japan); get_data_dictionary defines them per market. The source licences require each reply's `attribution` and `licence` notices to accompany the figures.

tools.name: get_group_structure
tools.description: A summary of one entity's place in the group-structure file (GLEIF relationship records, golden copy): whether the file holds a current direct and a current ultimate accounting consolidating parent for it, and how many current direct subsidiaries it has there, with the golden-copy date. Summary only, the same for every key: no names, LEIs, register numbers, periods or percentages; the reply says how the relationships themselves are supplied. The file covers relationships where the child or the parent has its legal address in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy or Spain. Input: id, a ticker (e.g. FOXF, or a register-number ticker such as 493455042.FR) or a 20-character LEI.
